decisions.decision: Use queue-fronted online serving for transaction scores
decisions.context: Scores must be returned during authorization in tens of milliseconds, including at peak load.
decisions.rationale: A distributed online scoring cluster behind a queue fits synchronous scoring and peak traffic. “Architecting a Machine Learning Pipeline: How to build scalable Machine Learning systems - Part 2/2” describes this pattern for load balancing, throughput, and low latency.
consequences: Queueing and serving capacity need operational management.
The authorization path depends on the serving cluster.

decisions.decision: Expose predictions through a REST microservice
decisions.context: The authorization system needs a synchronous interface to request a fraud score and receive it within its latency budget.
decisions.rationale: A prediction service provides the authorization application a direct request-response interface. “How to power up your product by machine learning with python microservice, pt. 1” and “Architecting a Machine Learning Pipeline: How to build scalable Machine Learning systems - Part 2/2” document API-backed prediction services.
consequences: The API contract becomes part of the authorization integration.
Network and service time consume the scoring budget.

decisions.decision: Serve prepared features from an online feature pipeline
decisions.context: Online scoring needs transaction features available quickly; the brief does not specify how those features are stored or retrieved.
decisions.rationale: Materialized features in a low-latency store fit the synchronous scoring constraint. “Productionizing Machine Learning with a Microservices Architecture” describes a shared preparation pipeline and online feature serving.
consequences: Feature freshness and serving availability need monitoring.
Feature preparation must be aligned with model inputs.

decisions.decision: Track model, feature, and training lineage for each release
decisions.context: Auditors must be able to determine which model version and features produced a score; the brief requires traceability but gives no specific record format.
decisions.rationale: Integrated lifecycle metadata best supports identifying deployed model versions and their training context. “Continuous Intelligence: Moving Machine Learning Application into Production Reliably” and “MLOps Principles” describe traceability across artifacts, datasets, runs, and deployments.
consequences: Serving records need links to model and feature versions.
Metadata capture and retention add storage and operational work.

decisions.decision: Monitor service health and data quality in production
decisions.context: The service must remain available during peaks, while changes in inputs can affect fraud scoring. The brief does not prescribe an automatic model update policy.
decisions.rationale: Monitoring latency, uptime, dependencies, and input quality directly addresses service availability and scoring reliability. “Productionizing Machine Learning with a Microservices Architecture” and “MLOps Principles” cover service and data monitoring.
consequences: Operational thresholds and response procedures must be defined.
Monitoring alone does not determine retraining or score policy.

uncovered: Fraud model family, training and evaluation method, and score-to-authorization policy.
The specific explanation method and audit record schema, including feature values per score.
Feature freshness and fallback behavior when online features are unavailable.
Availability targets, recovery objectives, capacity limits, and deployment topology.
